note: Phase 1 drawing test (2026-10-02), revised the same day after John's review. Read by tools/contact_sheet.py. Credits and licences are in ../research/play-image-plan.json. The failed Iphigenia at Aulis test stays in rejected/ and off the sheet.

drawings.name: Aeschylus · the Pythia (Eumenides)
drawings.alt: The Pythia, Apollo's priestess, fleeing in terror with her hands raised
drawings.source: Bötticher's 1859 drawing of an Apulian krater, Orestes at Delphi (Heidelberg scan, public domain)
drawings.method: Engraved plate: cut along her own lines, with straight cuts across blank paper; Apollo's overlapping foot erased; potrace
drawings.verdict: Clean. Revised twice: arm, head curl, fingers, knee edge and the whole shawl are in. One line is drawn in: her dress's black stripe, continued 45px across the gap where Apollo's foot was erased.

drawings.name: Sophocles · Euphorbos carrying the infant Oedipus
drawings.alt: The shepherd Euphorbos carrying the infant Oedipus on his shoulder, a long spear in his hand
drawings.source: Achilles Painter neck-amphora, Cabinet des médailles 372, four photographs by ArchaiOptix (CC BY-SA 4.0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photos taken off the vase (a fitted model of the vase and cameras, flattened without shear); upper body from the close view, lower from the frontal; clay mask, lines by local contrast redrawn even; hand, faces and sandal drawn as snapped strokes; back of the neck drawn in; spear straight at full length; potrace
drawings.verdict: John, 2026-10-02, on the second round: 'You flattened it right to my eyes.' The head now matches the close photo he pointed to; the hat no longer grows out of his neck.

drawings.name: Euripides · Iphigenia (Iphigenia in Tauris)
drawings.alt: Iphigenia, priestess of Artemis, holding out a letter tablet and the temple key
drawings.source: 1849 lithograph of the Buckingham vase, Archäologische Zeitung Taf. XII (public domain)
drawings.method: Lithograph: lines by local contrast, cut along her own lines, potrace
drawings.verdict: Clean. Revised twice: forearm, key hand, chain, sandals, veil edge and the whole tablet are in. Pylades' fingertips on the tablet's far edge cannot be told apart at this scan's size.

drawings.name: Aristophanes · Mika (Women at the Thesmophoria)
drawings.alt: Mika, in a comic old woman's mask, holding out a bowl
drawings.source: Würzburg krater H 5697, photograph by ArchaiOptix (CC BY-SA 4.0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo: clay mask, fold lines by local contrast, Mnesilochus' knife cut away, potrace
drawings.verdict: Clean. Revised: the drapery folds now run their full length. The painter's own drawing is sparer than the engravings.

drawings.name: Medea · in the serpent chariot
drawings.alt: Medea in a chariot drawn by two serpents
drawings.source: Cleveland Museum of Art 1991.1, museum photograph, full-resolution TIFF (CC0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo: clay mask, disk border cut away, netted sleeves kept; lines from the full-resolution TIFF; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable. Revised twice: the face and the netted left sleeve now show, and in dark mode the goad and the gaps inside the figure carry the clay. Still the busiest drawing.

drawings.name: Oedipus Tyrannus · Oedipus at the messenger's news
drawings.alt: Oedipus, bearded, in a long embroidered robe, his hand at his beard, holding a staff
drawings.source: Sicilian calyx-krater, Syracuse, Museo Paolo Orsi 66557, photograph by Dan Diffendale (CC BY-NC-SA 2.0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo: loose cut through the glaze, hand-drawn zones for floor, plaster, shoes and head; cracks erased; staff redrawn as a straight rod; hair and beard drawn solid, face lines evened; potrace
drawings.verdict: Usable. Revised after John's review: the head was crude; now the hair and a fuller beard are solid, the face lines even. The hem and shoes are worn on the vase and stay rough.

drawings.name: Antigone · Antigone bound, before Creon
drawings.alt: Antigone, veiled, her hands bound behind her back, her head bowed
drawings.source: Darius Painter amphora, Berlin F 3240, photograph by ArchaiOptix (CC BY-SA 4.0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photo taken off the vase (a fitted model, flattened without shear); clay mask; lines by local contrast redrawn even; hands and face from John's traces; eye from the paint; mends erased, folds joined; potrace
drawings.verdict: John, 2026-10-03: 'Antigone looking pretty good.' Clothes approved on the second pass; hands and face from his traces. Open: a dark spot on her upper arm, and the double jaw line in dark mode.

drawings.name: Philoctetes · Philoctetes on Lemnos
drawings.alt: Philoctetes alone on Lemnos, seated on a rock, his bandaged leg drawn up, his bow case beside him
drawings.source: Squat lekythos in the manner of the Eretria Painter, Met 56.171.58, photographs by Marie-Lan Nguyen (CC BY 2.5) and the Met (CC0)
drawings.method: Red-figure photos taken off the vase (a fitted model, flattened over the scene only); him, the rock and the bow case cut out as one, the tree cut off; lines found by their narrowness, washes left out, only black lines on the rock; head from John's trace; half tone on hair and beard; potrace
drawings.verdict: Fourth pass, 2026-10-03: head from John's trace, half tone on hair and beard (his asks); the hands are to follow his traces.
